_about: Hand-built ground truth for the keeper rules engine, reviewed by the commissioner.
The Keepers workbook cannot supply this: its Fee Allocations tabs are live VLOOKUPs, so
their K*_sal cells recompute against today's roster and render current-year numbers
against old declared fees. They are not a record of what anyone actually paid.
Every expected value here is a literal. Do not compute it from a formula in a test.

confirmed: A keeper fee sticks to the base permanently — it is paid again every season the player is kept, not once.
Zero keepers owes $0. The rules doc only enumerates 1/2/3.
Every sheet-anchored value below matches the commissioner's own reading of the workbook.

chains.why: Confirmed by Kevin. Acquired off waivers at $0. No tax on a first keep, so 2024 is free; the tax then rolls into the base each year. Today's ESPN base of $5 is his 2025 salary, which is the whole point of the ratchet.

A fee paid in year 1 is not a one-off charge: it becomes part of the base and is paid again every year after. This is the case the spreadsheet could never show, because it re-read the base from ESPN each year.
Kept at $30, dropped mid-season, re-added off waivers for $4. The tax is cleared and the base becomes the new acquisition value. The chain deliberately does NOT ratchet across the drop.

chains.case: prospect keep does not tax the following year
chains.why: Kept as a 2024 prospect at $12. In 2025 he shows Kept=FALSE and is absent from the kept_last_year list, so no tax follows — same pattern as Tyjae Spears. NOTE: the 2025 link is hypothetical. Belichick's Spy kept ARSB/McLaurin/LaPorta + Braelon Allen that year, so Johnston was rostered but not claimed. The $12 base is real and is what he would have cost.

Keepers tab shows $37 = 32+5. The -$1 leg. Nets to zero against JSN.

overrides.why: Once ESPN is restored the override is history and ESPN's value wins again.

Brian Thomas Jr., acquired by trade Oct 29 2025 and still taxed. The tax follows the player, not the roster.
Zach Charbonnet / Tyjae Spears / Tank Bigsby all kept at $3.
Priced at bare base regardless. The stray fee is reported as FEE_ON_PROSPECT rather than silently charged.

validation.case: base does not match prior salary
fees do not sum to tier

validation.why: A player has ONE rookie season, so a repeat prospect claim is a rule 1 violation detectable from the league's OWN claims, with no external source. It is now a cross-check on the draft-class rule rather than a substitute for it, and it stays ERROR while that one is REVIEW: the league's own record blocks, an outside data source flags. Applied from 2026 only -- the league previously allowed second-year prospects, which is why Tyjae Spears is legitimately a prospect in both 2024 and 2025 (commissioner, 2026-07-30).

validation.case: prospect ESPN has no draft class for
validation.why: Rule 1 was applied and could not be answered: ESPN carries neither draft.year nor debutYear for this player. A check that cannot run is reported, never passed -- silence reads exactly like success. Distinct from passing no mapping at all, which means the rule is not being applied (a pre-2026 season).

validation.case: prospect whose NFL career began before last season
validation.why: Rule 1: a prospect must be a rookie. first_nfl_season comes from ESPN's core API (draft.year, the draft class; debutYear for the undrafted). elapsed = claim.season - first_nfl_season, and > 1 is the violation -- NOT + 1, which would reject a genuine rookie like Cam Skattebo (began 2025, kept 2026). REVIEW rather than ERROR because the draft class comes from outside the league, so the final call is the commissioner's (commissioner, 2026-08-01).
